transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Well... I’ve started having these beliefs that something is going on behind the scenes at work, and even when people tell me it’s not true, I can’t shake the feeling. It’s making it really hard to even show up for my shifts, and my sister was worried enough that she convinced me to come in.
Can you tell me more about these beliefs you're having, are they so strong that you're completely convinced they're true, even if others show you evidence to the contrary?

I'm convinced my managers and a couple of the servers are running some kind of experiment on me, like changing my table sections or ticket times on purpose to see how I react. Even when they show me the schedule and swear it's all random, I still walk away absolutely sure there’s a hidden plan I'm not supposed to know about. I just can't shake the feeling that it's real, no matter what they tell me.
Have you experienced any other unusual thoughts or perceptions, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others don't, alongside these beliefs about the experiment at work?

Yes, I do. Pretty often when I'm alone in my apartment after a shift, I hear this low male voice calmly commenting on what I'm doing, like saying "you messed that up" when I'm checking sales numbers. I know no one else is there and the TV is off, but I still hear it.
Can you tell me more about how long you've been experiencing these voices and beliefs, and have they been continuous or have they come and gone over time?

They started about a year and a few months ago, shortly after I got back from my trip, and they've been pretty constant ever since. Even during a brief stretch late last summer when my mood and appetite picked up for a bit, the voice and the feeling that I was being tested kept going continuously for at least a couple of weeks.

Have you noticed any significant disorganization in your daily life, such as difficulty maintaining your personal appearance, or any unusual behavior that's out of character for you, since these beliefs and voices started?

My daily life has definitely become really disorganized, and though I still manage my personal appearance, my apartment is a total mess because I can't keep up with basic chores. I've also started doing unusual things like skipping work shifts just to stay home and stare at my notebooks, or sitting on the couch for hours unable to get myself to move.

Can you describe if you've experienced a lack of motivation or interest in activities you once enjoyed, or if you've had significant social withdrawal, beyond just the disorganization and unusual behaviors you've mentioned?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in things I used to love, like experimenting with new recipes. Now, I just come straight home from work to sit on the couch and stare at my notebooks, and I've been letting all my friends' and family's calls go to voicemail because I just can't bring myself to interact.
Can you describe how the voice you hear interacts with your beliefs about the experiment at work, does it comment on those beliefs or seem to be related to them in any way?

They actually feel pretty separate to me. The voice doesn't talk about the managers or the experiment, but instead just calmly comments on my own mistakes, like saying "you messed that up" when I'm checking sales numbers at home. The feeling of being tested is something that only happens while I'm actually at the restaurant.
Do you think the voice you hear is part of the experiment you believe is being conducted on you, or are they completely unrelated in your mind?

I'm not really sure if they are connected. I haven't really thought about whether the voice is actually part of the experiment at the restaurant, to be honest. They both just feel very real and overwhelming on their own, so I've just been dealing with them separately.
Have you ever considered that the voice you hear might be a part of your own mind, rather than an external entity, and how does that idea fit with your beliefs about the experiment at work?

I actually told my sister that I feel like I'm losing track of what's real and what's just in my head, but the voice sounds so distinct and unlike my own that it's hard to believe it's just my mind. It's like the experiment at work—even when people tell me it isn't real, I still can't shake that intense feeling that it is. It just makes it really hard to separate what's actually happening from what I'm thinking.

Can you describe if there are times when the voice you hear seems to be in response to your thoughts or actions, or if it ever comments on your beliefs about the experiment at work in a way that makes you question your own perceptions of reality?

The voice definitely comments on my actions, especially when I'm alone after a shift, like saying "you messed that up" while I'm checking my sales numbers. While it doesn't explicitly talk about the restaurant experiment, hearing it makes me feel deeply unsettled. It really contributes to that feeling of losing track of what is actually real versus what is just in my head.

Can you tell me if there are moments when you're completely convinced of the reality of the experiment and the voice, but then you have moments of doubt or questioning about whether these things are truly real, or if you're always completely certain they are real?

It’s a really confusing mix of both. On one hand, I try to rationalize it—like logically knowing no one is in my apartment when I hear the voice, or telling my sister I feel like I'm losing track of reality. But at the same time, the feeling is so strong that even when my managers show me the schedule to prove it's random, I still walk away completely convinced there's a hidden plan.

Can you describe if there are any times when you feel like you're able to step back and question the reality of the experiment or the voice, or if there are moments where you're completely caught up in these beliefs and can't consider alternative explanations?

Most of the time, I am completely caught up in these beliefs and just can't shake them. Even when my managers show me the schedule to prove it's random, I still walk away convinced there is a hidden plan. I've even told my sister that I feel like I'm losing track of what is real and what is just in my head.

Can you think of any situation or evidence that could possibly make you question or change your belief about the experiment at work, or do you feel that nothing could ever convince you that it's not real?

Honestly, I feel like nothing could fully convince me otherwise because the feeling is just too strong to shake. Even when my managers physically show me the schedule or swear everything is random, I still walk away absolutely certain there is a hidden plan. It just feels so real in the moment that logical explanations don't seem to change how I feel.

Have you ever experienced a period where your beliefs about the experiment at work and the voice you hear seemed to lessen or disappear, only to return later, or have they been consistently present since they started?

No, they haven't really disappeared and come back; they've been pretty constant. Ever since I returned from my trip about a year and a few months ago, both the voice and the beliefs about work have been consistently there without letting up.

You've mentioned feeling like you're losing track of what's real and what's in your head, but you still can't shake the feeling that the experiment is real. Can you tell me if there are any moments where you're able to acknowledge that your beliefs about the experiment might be a product of your own mind, rather than an actual external reality?

In a general sense, I do have moments where I worry I'm losing track of reality, especially when I'm talking to my sister. But when it comes to the experiment at work, it feels almost impossible to shake because it is just so intense. Even when my managers show me the schedules and swear it's all random, I still walk away completely convinced there is a hidden plan.
Can you describe if there are any specific actions or rituals you feel compelled to perform in response to the voice or the beliefs about the experiment, and if so, how they make you feel?

I don't really have any specific rituals or actions that I feel forced to perform in response to them. Mostly, I just try to ignore the voice, walk away, or end up feeling frozen and retreating to my apartment. I don't do any kind of repetitive behaviors to make them stop.
Can you describe if your beliefs about the experiment at work and the voice you hear are interconnected in a complex way, or are they separate and distinct experiences for you?

They feel like separate experiences, but they both seem tied to my work and how I'm performing. The belief about the experiment only happens at the restaurant, while the voice happens when I'm alone at home criticizing me for messing up my sales numbers. They don't form some complex conspiracy, but they both make me feel constantly judged and tested.

Can you describe if there are any times when the voice you hear directly tells you that you are being experimented on at work, or if it ever comments on your beliefs about the experiment in a way that reinforces or challenges them?

No, the voice has never directly mentioned the experiment or commented on those beliefs. It mostly occurs when I'm alone at home, calmly critiquing my actions like saying "you messed that up" when I'm checking sales numbers. The belief about being experimented on is just a separate, strong feeling I experience while I'm at the restaurant.

Can you tell me if you've ever experienced a moment where the voice you hear and your beliefs about the experiment at work seemed to intersect or influence each other directly, or have they always remained separate in your experience?

They have always remained pretty separate, though they happen during the same periods and both make me feel like I'm constantly being watched or tested. The voice is just a calm comment at home like "you messed that up" when I'm checking sales, whereas the experiment involves physical things at work like managers changing my table sections. They don't directly feed into each other, but they definitely share that same overwhelming feeling.
Can you describe if there are any periods where you feel completely normal, without the voice or the beliefs about the experiment, or if these experiences are always present to some degree?

No, I haven't really had any periods where I felt completely normal or free of those experiences. They've been pretty constant for over a year, and even during a brief stretch late last summer when my mood and energy picked up, I still heard the voice and felt like my coworkers were running experiments on me.

Can you describe if there are any times when you feel like you're able to distinguish between your delusional beliefs about the experiment and reality, or if you're always completely convinced of the reality of these beliefs?

When I'm talking to my sister, I can sometimes admit that I might be losing track of what's real and what's in my head. But when I'm actually at work, I am completely convinced. Even if my managers show me the schedule to prove it's random, I still walk away absolutely sure there is a hidden plan that I just can't shake.
Can you describe if your beliefs about the experiment at work are organized into a coherent system or narrative, or if they seem more fragmented and disconnected?

To me, it feels like a very organized and specific plan rather than something random. I'm convinced my managers and a few servers are working together on a coordinated experiment, specifically targeting me by changing my table sections and ticket times on purpose to test how I react. It all fits together too perfectly to be disconnected.

Can you describe any moments where you have questioned the possibility that your beliefs about the experiment might be false, or if you've ever considered seeking outside help to verify the reality of these beliefs?

Even when my managers show me the schedule to prove it's random, I still can't shake the feeling that they are testing me. However, I did have a moment where I realized I was losing track of what's real and what's just in my head, which really scared me. That's why I finally talked to my sister and decided to seek professional help to figure out what's actually going on.
Can you tell me if you've ever had any other delusional beliefs beyond the experiment at work, such as feeling like you're in danger or that someone is controlling your thoughts?

No, I've never felt like I was in danger or that anyone was trying to control my thoughts. My suspicious feelings are strictly focused on the restaurant, specifically the belief that my managers and coworkers are running that secret experiment on me.
Can you tell me if you have ever experienced a break from reality where you lost touch with your surroundings and your beliefs about the experiment seemed to fade away, even if only for a short time?

No, those beliefs about the experiment haven't ever really faded away, and they've been pretty constant for over a year now. Even during a brief couple of weeks last summer when my mood and energy picked up, the paranoia about being tested and that low male voice remained just as strong and felt completely real.
Can you describe if you have ever experienced any other organized delusional systems or beliefs beyond the experiment at work, or if this is the only one that you are convinced of?

Yes, this is the only one I have. I don't experience any other beliefs or systems like this outside of work, but this specific feeling that my managers and coworkers are running an experiment on me is incredibly persistent and feels completely real.
Have you ever experienced a moment where the voice you hear directly reinforces or confirms your beliefs about the experiment at work, making you even more convinced of its reality?

No, the voice doesn't directly talk about the experiment itself. It just criticizes my actions, like saying "you messed that up" when I'm alone at home. I haven't really thought about it reinforcing the experiment since they've always felt like separate things.
Can you describe if there are any times when you feel like the voice you hear is commanding you to do something specific, or if it's more of a commentary on your actions?

No, it never commands me to do anything. It's just a calm commentary on what I'm doing, specifically pointing out my mistakes, like saying "you messed that up" when I'm alone in my apartment checking sales numbers.
Can you tell me if your delusional beliefs about the experiment at work have ever changed or evolved over time, or have they remained relatively consistent since they first started?

They have remained very consistent ever since they started about a year and a few months ago, right after my trip. I've constantly believed that my managers and some servers are running this experiment on me by changing my table sections or ticket times on purpose. Even when they show me proof that it's random, that feeling never changes or goes away.
Can you describe if you have ever experienced a clear break from your delusional beliefs about the experiment, where you realized they might not be true, even if only for a short period?

No, I've never really had a clear break from those beliefs. Even when my managers and coworkers show me proof like the schedule and tell me it's not true, I still can't shake the feeling. I always walk away convinced that there is a hidden experiment going on.
